nodes.label: Migration Review Rule (RLS/rollback/FK index)
nodes.rationale: Flags missing RLS policies on new tables, destructive changes without a safe rollback path, and missing indexes on foreign keys.

nodes.label: App Router Component Review Rule
nodes.rationale: Flag missing loading/error boundaries, client/server component boundary mistakes, and unhandled Supabase query errors.

nodes.label: Server Action Review Rule (zod/auth)
nodes.rationale: Flag missing input validation (zod), missing auth/permission checks, and unhandled errors surfaced to the client.

nodes.label: Job Queue Worker GitHub Actions Workflow
repository_dispatch Trigger (run-worker)
nodes.rationale: Fired by lib/jobs/trigger-worker.ts right after an upload or board-pack click, so extraction starts within seconds. Primary path.

nodes.label: Scheduled Backstop Trigger (every 3h)
nodes.rationale: Sparse safety net retrying jobs left running by a killed run, and covers self-rescheduling board_pack/flags_run jobs.

nodes.label: Single-Drain Concurrency Guard
nodes.rationale: Never run two drains at once; queue a new trigger behind a run in progress rather than cancelling it mid-extraction.

nodes.label: Invoice OCR & Verification System Technical Spec
Two Extraction Paths (OCR parser vs Claude vision)
nodes.rationale: Route machine-printed GST invoices to a cheap dedicated OCR parser; route handwritten/messy or low-confidence invoices to Claude vision, which handles messy layouts and can flag its own uncertainty.

nodes.label: Claude API Integration Design
nodes.rationale: Use tool_use/function-calling schema to force structured JSON extraction rather than parsing free text, for reliable consistent fields.

nodes.label: Nightly Batch API Processing
nodes.rationale: Daily verification cadence suits async Batch API: ~50% cheaper, completes within an hour, matches non-instant review cadence.

nodes.label: Nightly Flagging Pass (cluster/duplicate/rate-drift/benchmark)
nodes.rationale: Separate nightly Claude call over structured rows (not raw images) mirrors the manual checks already done by hand, run automatically and incrementally.

nodes.label: Vendor-Matching / Clustering Logic
nodes.rationale: Fuzzy-match on phone/address/GSTIN-prefix; never auto-merge vendor identities without staff confirmation since it affects payment routing.

nodes.label: Staff Review Workflow (queue/screen/flags/sign-off/audit)
nodes.rationale: Queue sorted by risk (open flags, low confidence, high amount) so the highest-risk least-certain most-material items are reviewed first.

nodes.label: Reporting Outputs (rate card, cluster summary, flags digest, burn rate)
v1 Corrections (six load-bearing claims fixed)
nodes.rationale: v1 claimed every schema decision was cross-checked against real files; six claims failed against the actual export/master.xlsx files and were corrected.

nodes.label: Separate, Non-FK-Linked Classification Dimensions Decision
nodes.rationale: admin_head (42 Venue Setup items), budget_head (10 import-derived heads) and cost_center (cross-department Tally-style list) hold completely different data and share only the role of hand-assigned enrichment; kept as separate tables/columns with no FK relationship, ever.

nodes.label: Vendor Resolution Rule (normalize, match, never auto-merge)
nodes.rationale: Never fuzzy-auto-merge vendor identities; merging affects payment routing and stays a human decision. Automatic clustering detection cut to week 2; identity capture starts day 2.

nodes.label: ubbl_number Normalization Rule
nodes.rationale: normalizeId() rejects non-finite/decimals, truncates numbers, trims strings, unit-tested against both shapes, so integer vs string UBBL numbers don't break the unique key across import runs.

nodes.label: UBBL/Main-Number Namespace Collision Check
nodes.rationale: ADP_202608054 appears as both a UBBL Number and a Main Entry Number on different rows; the importer asserts no value exists in both columns and raises a high exception if it does.

nodes.label: Dry-Run-First Import Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every import runs dry_run first inside a rolled-back transaction, showing a per-row diff before commit. A finance import that applies blind is a defect, not a feature.

nodes.label: Hub-Owned Columns Excluded From Import Upsert
nodes.rationale: admin_head_id/zone_id/cost_center_id/status tracking columns are deliberately absent from the upsert's SET clause so a re-import can never silently revert a staff verification decision.

nodes.label: Status Export Outward Flow (file-based, permanent, no API)
nodes.rationale: The only place data flows outward. DESCOPED 2026-08-13: permanently a generated .xlsx applied by hand on the other side; format='api' left in the CHECK constraint but never written, since removing an unused enum value is pure churn.

nodes.label: _ocr/_verified Twin-Column Pattern
nodes.rationale: Non-destructive by construction: edited fields write only to _verified columns; _ocr is never mutated, preserving both the machine read and the human correction.

nodes.label: Audit Trail / No-Silent-Overwrite Rule
nodes.rationale: v1 stored only the last writer (updated_by), which is a silent overwrite the original tech spec's audit-trail requirement explicitly forbids; entry_change_log stores every from/to change plus actor and source.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED Claiming Pattern
nodes.rationale: Ordinary Postgres, no extension or vendor lock; safe across any number of concurrent workers. Stuck 'running' rows are reclaimed by a sweeper and retried with backoff, then marked dead after max_attempts.

nodes.label: Identical Handler Code, Two Callers Pattern
nodes.rationale: Vercel Cron calls /api/jobs/tick today; a Windows Service runs worker/index.ts continuously later. Identical handler code in lib/jobs/handlers/ — only the caller differs, making server migration a configuration change.

nodes.label: security_invoker Reporting Views Requirement
nodes.rationale: A Postgres view bypasses RLS by default, running as its creator; security_invoker=true makes it run as the calling user so table RLS policies still apply, preventing cross-department leakage in reports.

nodes.label: Nonce-Based Content Security Policy (proxy.ts/middleware.ts)
nodes.rationale: Set once in the app, never at the proxy/IIS, because browsers apply the intersection of duplicate CSP headers; nonce-based because 'unsafe-inline' defeats CSP's purpose; requires dynamic rendering.

nodes.label: Review Queue Keyboard-First Design
nodes.rationale: Throughput per reviewer is the product's real KPI; queue ordered by open-exception severity, extraction confidence, then amount. Keyboard contract removes mouse dependency for the common path.

nodes.label: Gold Set Regression Harness (21 invoices)
nodes.rationale: 90-second deterministic pipeline run against 21 fixed, blind-labelled invoices — the only way to tell whether a prompt change helped, hurt, or did nothing; catches silent misses a correction log cannot.

nodes.label: Correction Log Discovery Mechanism
nodes.rationale: A view over the never-overwritten _ocr/_verified columns surfaces real-world failure classes at scale, but is anchored (reviewers accept wrong pre-filled values more often) and cannot A/B a prompt.

nodes.label: OCR Improvement Loop (no automatic learning)
nodes.rationale: Corrections accumulate → /accuracy surfaces patterns → human edits prompt/schema → re-run gold set to catch regressions → deploy. The model is never fine-tuned by corrections.

nodes.label: Tech Stack Decision (Next.js/Supabase/Node worker)
nodes.rationale: Route Handlers plus a plain Node worker chosen over Supabase Edge Functions because Deno Edge Functions cannot run on the eventual Windows Server; plain Node runs anywhere.

nodes.label: Dashboard Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Group by meaning not data source; every number implies an action or all-clear; scale visual weight to urgency; plain language over jargon; legible at a glance on a phone.

nodes.label: Brand Personality (plain, calm, trustworthy)
nodes.rationale: Quiet confidence: state numbers and status directly, no hype, no decorative flourishes competing with the data; not a generic SaaS analytics dashboard.

nodes.label: Static-Optimization Nonce Bug (/login had zero nonces)
nodes.rationale: Next's automatic static optimization silently prerendered /login at build time with no per-request nonce, so every script was blocked and React never hydrated under enforced CSP.

nodes.label: pg_trgm Installed In Public Schema Warning
Schema Drift Incident (4 unapplied migrations)
nodes.rationale: tsc/ESLint/unit tests all passed because Supabase column names are untyped string literals; static checks validate code against a schema they never consult, so an unapplied migration silently broke /review.

nodes.label: Shared-Master-Per-Event-Membership Pattern
nodes.rationale: One row per real department/head/zone forever plus a join table for per-event membership, rather than copying rows per event, which would recreate the fuzzy-matching trap vendor/vendor_alias already exists to avoid.

nodes.label: Hub Status Clarification (Status/Audit status/Hub status)
nodes.rationale: An entry carries three independent status fields; Hub status is the only one this app writes and the only thing ever exported back out.

nodes.label: Leaked Tool-Call Syntax In OCR Fields (diagnosed)
nodes.rationale: strict:true tool calling guarantees valid JSON structure but not field content; a momentary hallucination of Claude's own tag formatting can leak into a text field value.

nodes.label: Bill→Entry Linking Improvement (department-scoped, manifest invoice-number priority)
Hub Screen Certification — Audit & Remediation Plan
Review Queue Nondeterministic Order Bug (1.1)
nodes.rationale: The queue sorts on severity, confidence, amount and stops with no final tiebreaker, so ties (the common case) return in arbitrary Postgres order, making bill position and LIMIT 500 unstable.

nodes.label: Exceptions Queue Unordered/Unlimited Fetch Bug (1.2)
nodes.rationale: Sorting happens client-side after an unordered, unlimited fetch, so PostgREST's default cap can silently truncate high-severity exceptions on an audit tool — the worst available failure mode.

nodes.label: Vendor Search Parentheses 400 Bug (1.4)
nodes.rationale: PostgREST reserves parentheses as or() group delimiters; a vendor name like 'Acme (India)' closes the filter group early and 400s, though such names are ordinary in Indian vendor data.

nodes.label: Review Claim Race/Never-Released/Never-Enforced Bug (1.8)
nodes.rationale: Claim is a read-then-write race, never released on leave, never refreshed on multi-bill navigation, and never checked by saveVerification, so two reviewers can both save the same bill with last-write-wins.

nodes.label: Unified Status Colour Map (3.3)
nodes.rationale: 'Pending' renders grey on Entries via label-sniffing but amber on the Dashboard via a code-first map; the two should be unified into one shared lib/status-badge.ts.

nodes.label: D1: Bill→Entry Attach Writes To A Column Nothing Reads
nodes.rationale: attachExtractionToEntry writes document_extraction.entry_id but review/page.tsx and v_review_queue read source_document.entry_id, so attach 'succeeds' in the UI and changes nothing observable.

nodes.label: D3: Bare R Destroys Unsaved Corrections
nodes.rationale: An unmodified 'r' keypress runs Sonnet re-extraction with no confirmation or dirty check, remounting the form and silently discarding twenty typed corrections while billing a Sonnet call.

nodes.label: D4: Multi-Bill PDF Collapses To One Arbitrary Bill
nodes.rationale: A Map keyed by source_document_id keeps only the last document_extraction row per document, so a multi-bill PDF displays and links only one bill in the inbox.

nodes.label: D5: Upload Blocks On Backlog; Timeout Reported As Failure
nodes.rationale: The ingest route drains unrelated queued jobs after this document's own job before responding, and a platform timeout is reported as upload failure even though extraction likely succeeded.

nodes.label: D6: Inbox Re-runs Its Heaviest Query Every 4s
nodes.rationale: router.refresh() on a 4s interval re-executes six queries including entries capped at 5,000 rows plus candidate ranking, with no loading state to show for it.

nodes.label: D7: Import Commit Has No Progress And No Timeout Ceiling
D8: No Visible Signal When The Queue Stops Draining
C1: Always-Present Three-State Entry Match Strip
Z1: Zone+Admin-Head As Stage 3 Of Review Flow
Z2: Zone+Admin-Head At Moment Of Attach
L3: Confidence Tint Carries No Signal
nodes.rationale: Confidence is stored per run not per field, so one tintClass paints every input; colour that is always on carries no information and trains reviewers to ignore red exactly where it matters.

nodes.label: V1: Validation, Dirty State, Save Conflicts
INGEST_INLINE_EXTRACTION Decision (superseded 2026-09-05)
nodes.rationale: Originally kept on because staff upload/review from multiple locations and a local worker or laptop would be a single point of failure; superseded once Vercel Hobby's real 10s hard-kill (not the declared 60s maxDuration) was confirmed, so inline became the slow failing path and now defaults to false.

nodes.label: Job Queue Worker on GitHub Actions
Repository Dispatch Token Setup (instant trigger)
nodes.rationale: Without a fine-grained PAT wired to Vercel, extraction still works but waits up to 3 hours for the scheduled run instead of starting within seconds.

nodes.label: Actions-Minutes Budget Plan
nodes.rationale: Private-repo free tier is 2,000 min/month; scheduled backstop plus upload-triggered runs land comfortably under it at ~30-40 docs/day, with widening the schedule or going public as fallback levers.

nodes.label: Where OCR Should Execute — Decision Doc
Option A: Chunked Continuation (resumable per-page extraction)
nodes.rationale: Process as many pages as fit the request budget, return a partial result, client requests the next chunk; document_page already records per-page verdicts so 'which pages remain' is a query, not new state.

nodes.label: Option B: Always-On Worker Machine
nodes.rationale: worker/index.ts already exists with no timeout; ruled out as primary because the available machine sleeps or gets shut off, and a silently-stopped worker is worse than none.

nodes.label: Option C: GitHub Actions As Genuine Executor
nodes.rationale: Trigger via repository_dispatch and run extraction inside the runner itself (not curl Vercel); removes the page ceiling via the 6-hour runner limit but a 30-60s cold start fails the instant-start requirement.

nodes.label: Option D: Vercel Pro (raise maxDuration to 300s)
nodes.rationale: Effectively a one-line change moving the page ceiling from ~30 to ~150 pages for $20/month; moves the ceiling rather than removing it.

nodes.label: Measured Extraction Time Ceiling (~25-30 pages inline)
nodes.rationale: A real 8-page bundle measured ~15s wall clock at 4-page concurrency; 50 pages extrapolates to ~100s and times out, so the practical inline ceiling is 25-30 pages.

nodes.label: Staged Recommendation (D now, measure, then A if needed)
nodes.rationale: Take option D immediately for cheap relief, measure the real maximum bundle size against the new ~150-page ceiling, and only build option A's chunked continuation if that measurement says it is needed.

nodes.label: Speed, Efficiency & UX Remediation — Execution Plan
Reports / Settings / Workload — Redesign Execution Plan
Review & Documents Inbox Redesign — Final Plan
OCR System — Full Review, Issue List, and Remediation Plan
Three-role model (Dept/Admin/Superadmin)
nodes.rationale: Replaces an earlier Viewer/Reviewer/Admin model that never shipped; write actions (Review, enrichment edits, Hub status, exception resolution) are deliberately restricted to admin-or-above so verifying/resolving stays a considered action, not a Dept-level default.

nodes.label: Import dry-run-then-commit pattern
nodes.rationale: Nothing is written until Commit is clicked, so a wrong column guess or bad batch is visible and free to abandon; once committed a batch is permanent and cannot be undone by re-running.

nodes.label: Audit portal bookmarklet scraper
nodes.rationale: A drag-to-bookmarks-bar token-based reader that submits the Audit portal's on-screen table to the Hub without ever holding the portal password; token shown once, expires in 30 days.

nodes.label: Import-before-scrape ordering requirement
nodes.rationale: The Audit portal's Entry Number only matches a Hub entry because today's Departmental import just wrote that number onto it; scraping first makes every row an unmatched exception (recoverable, not damaging, but wastes the pass).

nodes.label: Hub status export batch workflow
nodes.rationale: The only way Awaiting Verification/Awaiting Validation decisions leave the Hub; a generated batch is permanent and never rewritten, so a wrong batch is fixed by process, not by regenerating.

nodes.label: Required note on exception resolve/dismiss
nodes.rationale: A note explaining why is mandatory on every status change and every exception resolution so a later reader can understand the decision without re-deriving it.

nodes.label: Never edit the database directly
nodes.rationale: Every change must go through app screens so a required note, an audit trail, and the correct permission check all happen together.

nodes.label: getCachedUser() memoized auth lookup
nodes.rationale: React cache() dedupes auth.getUser() per request; takes no arguments and builds its own client internally because cache() dedupes by argument identity and each call site previously built a fresh client, which would defeat the cache.

nodes.label: getCachedStaffProfile() memoized profile lookup
nodes.rationale: Keyed by userId; selects the superset of columns every call site needs so one cached query shape serves both the nav rail and role gates instead of two different .select() calls.

nodes.label: unstable_cache reference-data module
nodes.rationale: Caches the full unfiltered lookup tables (department, budget_head, admin_head, zone, cost_center, entry_status, hub_status) with per-call-site JS filtering, so RLS-varying tables and event-membership filtering both stay correct without needing the cache key to vary by role or event.

nodes.label: RLS non-uniformity across reference tables
nodes.rationale: admin_head/zone/budget_head gate through can_see_department() and differ by role, so a single global cache key would leak or truncate rows across roles; fixed by keying those three fetchers on userId.

nodes.label: Lazy-loaded PDF viewer on Review
nodes.rationale: next/dynamic with ssr:false and a module-resolving .then() form lets pdf.js load only once a bill is opened, while keeping the forwardRef used for keyboard navigation intact.

nodes.label: Login error routed through FriendlyError
nodes.rationale: Brought the login screen's error rendering in line with the app-wide toast/FriendlyError pattern since it is the first screen every person sees.

nodes.label: No self-serve or admin password reset (gap)
nodes.rationale: createStaffUser only sets a password at account creation and rejects re-creating an existing ITS number; no admin password lever existed, an undocumented gap rather than a deliberate design choice.

nodes.label: resetStaffPassword admin action
nodes.rationale: Superadmin-gated action using createAdminClient().auth.admin.updateUserById to bypass RLS, closing the forgot-password gap with an in-app lever while leaving self-serve reset as future/out-of-band.

nodes.label: 390px mobile static responsive audit
nodes.rationale: Done as a code-based static audit rather than a real device test since no browser/device tool was available; nav rail's unconditional expanded width was the single highest-impact finding.

nodes.label: Nav rail narrow-viewport auto-collapse
nodes.rationale: useSyncExternalStore + matchMedia ORs into effectiveCollapsed so a phone always gets the icon-only rail regardless of saved desktop preference, avoiding the hydration-flicker pattern of useEffect+useState.

nodes.label: Root cause A: unindexable OR lateral join in v_review_queue
nodes.rationale: Postgres cannot flatten a correlated OR across two columns, so the exception scan re-plans per outer row against indexes not scoped to status='open' — the dominant cost on every /review load.

nodes.label: Root cause B: whole-ledger fuzzy matching in request path
nodes.rationale: Up to 5,000 entries rows fetched and ranked in JS on every unmatched-bill open, causing silent truncation of older entries and RLS multiplier cost.

nodes.label: Root cause C: getSelectedEventId never memoized
nodes.rationale: Every call site re-issued two round trips (cookie validate + row fetch); nine call sites on /reports alone.

nodes.label: v_review_queue CTE rewrite (migration 20260904000001)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the correlated lateral OR with two pre-aggregated, UNION'd CTEs to avoid double-counting a reconciliation_exception row that carries both entry_id and document_extraction_id, discovered as a real reachable bug via flagReviewException.

nodes.label: match_candidate_entries server-side RPC
nodes.rationale: SECURITY INVOKER function pre-filtering by vendor, amount proximity, normalized invoice number and vendor-name trigram similarity before ranking, replacing an unbounded 5,000-row entries fetch and its silent-truncation correctness bug; a LIMIT 300 exists only as a last-resort safety valve, not the primary bound.

nodes.label: Threading eventId through reports loaders
nodes.rationale: Avoids each loader re-reading the cookie once the page already resolved the event; cheaper to fix before more unimported loaders replicate the pattern.

nodes.label: Superadmin self-lockout guard
nodes.rationale: Blocks a superadmin from demoting or deactivating their own account without explicit confirmation, enforced both client-side (Dialog confirmation) and server-side in updateStaffProfile.

nodes.label: Middleware matcher excludes pdf.worker.min.mjs / bookmarklet
nodes.rationale: Opening a bill previously triggered a full middleware run (CSP nonce + auth.getUser()) just to serve a static worker script, in the review flow's most latency-sensitive moment.

nodes.label: INGEST_INLINE_EXTRACTION flag and Hobby-tier maxDuration exposure
nodes.rationale: Vercel Hobby hard-caps execution at 10s while inline synchronous extraction could run ~15s+, causing silent data loss; flipping the flag to false moved to a poll-based upload path already built (app/api/documents/status/route.ts).

nodes.label: GitHub Actions worker job drain (worker.yml)
nodes.rationale: cron-tick.yml's /api/jobs/tick ran the same extraction handler under the same 10s Hobby kill, so it was never a working safety net; the fix runs worker/index.ts directly as a GitHub Actions job with no Vercel function and a repository_dispatch trigger fired within seconds of work being queued.

nodes.label: Review workspace re-render elimination (Phase 5)
nodes.rationale: Splitting one large header-form useState object into per-field slices, memoizing heavy children, fixing an O(n^2) diff, replacing a JSON.stringify dirty check, and keying the PDF viewer on sourceDocumentId instead of documentExtractionId so sibling-bill navigation no longer remounts pdf.js.

nodes.label: Reports Suspense streaming restructuring (Phase 6.1)
nodes.rationale: Splits each surface's sections into small async Server Components behind their own Suspense boundary so hero metrics paint before the slowest section resolves, rather than one page-wide Promise.all gating all JSX.

nodes.label: Board pack status polling
nodes.rationale: Client-side polling with backoff chosen over revalidatePath/revalidateTag because the board-pack job can be driven by a standalone Node worker with no Next request context, where server-side revalidation would silently no-op.

nodes.label: Vendor merge confirmation step
nodes.rationale: Merging previously happened immediately on target selection with no confirmation despite re-attributing spend and document history; added a confirm step modeled on the Dialog-confirmation convention from the superadmin self-lockout guard.

nodes.label: Asymmetric JWT verification (deferred lever)
nodes.rationale: Would remove one to two real network hops from every request via getClaims() instead of auth.getUser() calling the Auth server, but requires enabling asymmetric signing keys, a project-level and possibly plan-gated decision, so deliberately not done.

nodes.label: Merged exceptions queue + severity-counts fetch (Phase 4.3)
nodes.rationale: Reuses the queue's own bucketed fetch as the severity chips' source only when it is provably the full open population, falling back to a separate fetch otherwise, while resolveEventIds always runs once per request regardless of which branch is taken.

nodes.label: Exceptions queue hides 33 of 34 open items (0.1)
nodes.rationale: Event-scoping /exceptions resolves each row's event only through entry_id and drops every row where that is null, discarding all document-level and batch-level exceptions since only one open exception has an entry_id.

nodes.label: Three screens disagree by 30x on exception count (0.2)
nodes.rationale: Dashboard reads v_open_issues unfiltered by event, Reports reads it filtered by event, Exceptions reads the base table with the 0.1 bug — three different resolution rules for the same underlying count.

nodes.label: reconciliation_exception has no source_document_id (0.3)
nodes.rationale: Ten open exceptions reference their document only inside free-text description, so they can never be attributed to an event or surfaced on a document's or entry's page.

nodes.label: Nothing drains the job queue in production (1.1)
nodes.rationale: Only local-dev-tick/local-dev-upload/e2e-drain workers have ever claimed a job; the GitHub Actions cron's one-time setup steps were never completed, so flags_run never runs and failed extractions never retry.

nodes.label: staff_department is empty (1.2)
nodes.rationale: RLS is department-based via can_see_department(); with zero staff_department rows and all accounts admin/superadmin, the department-role path (and its RLS) has never been exercised.

nodes.label: Department budget data never imported (1.4)
nodes.rationale: department_budget_allocation is empty and the import workspace's own code comment notes no real spreadsheet has been provided yet, so its column parsing is unverified against a real sheet shape.

nodes.label: approved_amount is zero on every budget head (1.5)
nodes.rationale: The Departmental import brings utilised figures but not approved ones; unclear whether the source export lacks approved amounts or the importer drops the column.

nodes.label: PDF opens on page 1, never on the bill's own page (2.1)
nodes.rationale: pageNumberStart is passed to extraction-form.tsx for a label but never to pdf-viewer.tsx, which hard-codes useState(1); the highest-value fix in the document.

nodes.label: 'Bill 4 of 3' impossible counter (2.2)
nodes.rationale: bill_index is the bill's absolute position but bill_count comes from v_review_queue, which contains only unverified bills, so the denominator drops as bills get verified while numerators stay absolute.

nodes.label: Save advances to queue's next bill, not next bill in this PDF (2.3)
nodes.rationale: The queue is ordered by severity/confidence/amount by design, so saving bill 1 of PDF-A can land on PDF-B rather than the next unverified sibling bill in the same document.

nodes.label: Documents inbox tracks extraction, not review (3.1)
nodes.rationale: Once a document reaches 'Extracted' the row stops changing forever regardless of how many of its bills remain unreviewed; the page never queries verified_at at all.

nodes.label: Entry page lists bills but never sums them (3.2)
nodes.rationale: linked-documents.tsx renders each bill's own OCR'd total with no sum and no comparison to the entry's imported amount, leaving the tally to be done by eye.

nodes.label: Mismatches never shown on the entry page (3.3)
nodes.rationale: The entry detail page has zero references to reconciliation_exception or flags; all open exceptions live only on the separate /exceptions list.

nodes.label: Nothing anywhere says a PDF is finished (3.4)
nodes.rationale: No 'complete' state exists in Review or Documents inbox; requires both the Save-recognizes-last-bill fix (2.3) and the verified_at-in-query fix (3.1) to agree on what complete means.

nodes.label: A flag tells you it is wrong, not what to do (4.1)
nodes.rationale: Resolving an exception opens only a free-text note dialog with no destination button routing to the thing that needs changing; proposed a one-line 'what to do' plus a link per exception type.

nodes.label: Nine exception types have no plain-English label (4.2)
nodes.rationale: EXCEPTION_TYPE_LABELS covers 14 of 20 database-allowed types; the missing nine render as raw snake_case codes and are also missing from the type filter since EXCEPTION_TYPES derives from the labels map.

nodes.label: Department to budget head to expense drilldown doesn't connect (5.1)
nodes.rationale: Budget heads render as one flat list across all departments with no department column and no link out, unlike department/vendor/zone rows which all link to a filtered Entries list.

nodes.label: Two vendor sections overlap (5.2)
nodes.rationale: Vendor spend and vendor concentration rank the same vendors by the same spend with the same bar chart, differing only in trailing columns; proposed folding into one table.

nodes.label: Cost centres appear nowhere in Reports, none assigned (5.4)
nodes.rationale: The middle rung of the department-cost_center-budget_head hierarchy the user described is missing entirely; the plumbing exists (a cost_center table, a filter, a picker) but nothing has ever been assigned.

nodes.label: Four surfaces missed event scoping (6.1)
nodes.rationale: Dashboard, v_entry_status_counts, the analytics views, and /import batch history all lack event_id; invisible today because only one event exists, but the Dashboard will start lying the day a second event is created.

nodes.label: No way to switch events (6.2)
nodes.rationale: A prior commit deleted event-switcher.tsx and setActiveEvent, so the active_event_id cookie is now written by nothing, making read-only past-event browsing unreachable.

nodes.label: Model commentary landing in a data field (10.1)
nodes.rationale: A bank cheque page's notes field contained prose about the document instead of content from it, and vendor was misread as the bank rather than the actual supplier, the same class of problem as the existing leaked-tag-syntax guard.

nodes.label: Prompt-cache fix sits 57 tokens from a silent cliff (10.2)
nodes.rationale: Claude Haiku 4.5's 4,096-token minimum cacheable prefix was measured at ~4,039 tokens, 57 short; prompts under the floor process without caching and without error, so a future prompt trim silently stops caching with nothing to notice.

nodes.label: No skip_reason for an ID document like a PAN card (10.3)
nodes.rationale: The skip_reason check constraint has no id_document value, so PAN/Aadhaar pages fall into the ambiguous 'other' bucket, indistinguishable from a genuinely unclassifiable page.

nodes.label: 20-page upload ceiling, needs a resumable-extraction decision
nodes.rationale: Measured 8 pages ~15s, 20 ~39s, 28 ~54s against a 60s limit; raising the cap needs either a longer request budget or resumable extraction, deferred pending the largest realistic weekly upload.

nodes.label: Department-level budget vs. actual (feature concept)
nodes.rationale: A separate, department-granularity budget dataset (not a rollup of per-budget-head allocations) hand-imported from Excel and compared against event actuals; specified fully in review-page-layout-redesign-plan.md §11.

nodes.label: Six-tag entry grain + line-item level
nodes.rationale: Every entry is tagged on six independent axes (department, admin head, zone, budget head/category, vendor, entry type) plus a line-item level beneath it; almost every report in the catalogue is a measure crossed with one or two of these tags, and the line-item level is what lets rates compare across vendors and time.

nodes.label: Report Family A — Budget & spend
nodes.rationale: What is missing is not totals but comparison — against budget over time, against pace, against last year, against each other.

nodes.label: Report Family B — Vendors
nodes.rationale: Vendor alias-merging and normalization make concentration, dependency and relationship analysis actually work rather than fragmenting across spelling variants.

nodes.label: Report Family C — What we bought
nodes.rationale: The line-item family is the part no conventional expense report can produce, because a rate is comparable in a way an invoice total never is.

nodes.label: Report Family D — Entry integrity
nodes.rationale: The controls already run and attach rupees to what they find; missing is the reporting layer turning 23 exception types and 14 flag types into a short actionable list.

nodes.label: Report Family E — Executive framings
nodes.rationale: No new data — arranges existing measures into shapes a decision-maker can act on in under a minute.

nodes.label: B-01 Concentration curve (flagship)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not a classic dual-axis Pareto chart, since two scales on one chart is the most common way a finance chart misleads.

nodes.label: C-04 Above-median overpayment (flagship)
nodes.rationale: (rate - median) x quantity, summed, produces a headline rupee figure benchmarked against the organization's own purchase history rather than an external one, very hard to argue with.

nodes.label: D-01 Exception heat map (flagship)
nodes.rationale: Sequential single-hue shading, never a rainbow, so darker always and only means more rupees at risk.

nodes.label: C-02 Purchase tree (flagship)
nodes.rationale: Item family to catalogue item to vendor to specific bills, drillable at every level — the only view answering 'what did we actually buy'.

nodes.label: C-09 Instrument-type mix (flagship)
nodes.rationale: Turns a compliance question (tax invoice vs letterhead bill vs cash memo) into a money question measured in rupees, not counts.

nodes.label: E-01 Department league table (flagship)
nodes.rationale: Ranking departments on budget adherence, projected landing, spend share, documentation coverage and rupees at risk changes behaviour in a way that reporting totals never does.

nodes.label: Executive Brief screen design
nodes.rationale: Composed to read top-to-bottom as an argument: position, what moved, where to look, what needs a decision — for trustees and senior administration in under thirty seconds.

nodes.label: Present mode feature
nodes.rationale: A full-screen, large-type, no-navigation rendering of the Brief for a projector — a stylesheet and a keyboard shortcut that is the difference between a web app and a presented report.

nodes.label: Board pack (PDF + workbook) concept
nodes.rationale: The Executive Brief rendered to a scheduled PDF and matching workbook, in the spreadsheet idiom the organisation already circulates widely.

nodes.label: Settings Direction A — plain fixed-order list
nodes.rationale: One plain fixed-order list of rows edited in place, no tabs/status strip/charts; structural areas become focused sub-routes, each keeping its own server-side role gate.

nodes.label: Fold Workload into Documents as a toggle
nodes.rationale: Superadmin-only Inbox/Workload segmented toggle on /documents replaces the separate nav item and route, with the old route redirecting rather than being removed.

nodes.label: Reports left-index + right-pane workspace
nodes.rationale: Pane rests on a per-surface overview (hero tiles, two flagship charts, disclosure); selecting a report swaps the pane to that section at full fidelity, with pinned '★ My reports' via a per-browser cookie.

nodes.label: Vendor email extraction field
nodes.rationale: Added the same way vendor phone/address already work, not a new email-ingestion channel.

nodes.label: COMMUNITY_GSTIN exclusion check
nodes.rationale: When the model reads the community's own GSTIN into vendor_gstin, isSameGstin nulls the field and raises a low-severity vendor_gstin_is_own_org exception.

nodes.label: Job-queue drain diagnosis (item 3)
nodes.rationale: Newly-uploaded PDFs never appeared for review because v_review_queue only lists documents with a document_extraction row, which only exists once something actively drains job_queue; an operational fact, not fixable from inside the codebase alone.

nodes.label: DocumentStageTracker staged progress component
nodes.rationale: Uploaded to Queued to Extracting to Done/Failed staged progress rather than a fake percentage, since no partial progress is obtainable from one non-streaming tool-use call.

nodes.label: manualExtractNow bypass action
nodes.rationale: Calls extractAndPersist directly, bypassing job_queue entirely, as a manual workaround for the drain diagnosis (item 3).

nodes.label: Documents table with client pagination (item 4)
nodes.rationale: Plain table on the existing table primitive rather than adopting the unused @tanstack/react-table dependency already sitting in package.json.

nodes.label: Collapsible sidebar auto-collapsed on /review (item 6)
nodes.rationale: A ref (not state) tracks a manual re-expand override during a /review visit so it doesn't itself trigger a re-render; entering /review force-collapses unless overridden, leaving restores the localStorage preference.

nodes.label: Command palette (Ctrl/Cmd-K search)
nodes.rationale: Built alongside item 6 but undocumented as its own item at the time; wires cmdk's Command.Dialog to the existing RLS-scoped searchEntriesForAttach search.

nodes.label: Bill navigation scoped to pending, not whole document set (§1)
nodes.rationale: A reviewer's mental model treats /review as 'next unreviewed bill', not a walk through already-verified history, so navigation defaults to the pending subset with an explicit Unverified/All toggle.

nodes.label: Merged Bill/Page/Sibling-bill navigation cluster (§2)
nodes.rationale: Three previously separate navigation locations become one card with adjacent groups; the flagged-field stepper is deliberately excluded since not every bill has flagged fields.

nodes.label: Actions bar: primary vs. occasional (§3)
nodes.rationale: Re-extract with Sonnet and Hub status move behind 'More' since Sonnet is a deliberately considered, costlier choice rather than a habitual click; keyboard shortcuts continue working regardless of menu placement.

nodes.label: One status line for Verify → Connect → Classify (§4)
nodes.rationale: Replaces a purely decorative three-chip progress indicator with one row carrying each stage's real control; drops the OCR-confidence badge since pairing it with a mismatch exception badge implied a relationship that doesn't exist.

nodes.label: Page-to-field OCR sync indicator (§6)
nodes.rationale: A real behavior gap, not just display: PdfViewer owns pageNumber independently of ExtractionForm, and the link from field to page was one-directional only; fixed by labeling each field with its source page.

nodes.label: Suggested-match UI simplified to one line (§7)
nodes.rationale: The evidence breakdown card duplicated information visible elsewhere; 'Not this?' relabeled since its real job is opening both ranked candidates and manual search, not dismissal.

nodes.label: Footer: two labeled comparison cards (§8)
nodes.rationale: Replaces hover-only tooltips most reviewers never click with permanent one-line captions on 'Bill math' and 'Compared to Entries'.

nodes.label: invoice_number as a weighted matching factor (§9)
nodes.rationale: Population check on real production data (11/11 document extractions, 11/14 entries) supported building it as a binary weighted factor (vendor 0.4, amount 0.2, date 0.15, invoice number 0.25) rather than an exact-match short-circuit, since legibility couldn't be judged from population alone.

nodes.label: Vendor alias/correction memory for matching (§10)
nodes.rationale: vendor/vendor_alias infrastructure already exists and is wired into Excel import; the gap is that document_extraction has no vendor_id, so matching never consults vendor_alias — fixed as a score-only, no-auto-fill deterministic signal layered next to fuzzy scoring, mirroring the invoice_number addition.

nodes.label: GST recipient-compliance check (§12)
nodes.rationale: A valid ITC-claimable tax invoice must show the recipient's GSTIN, name and invoice number; the compliance decision stays deterministic code comparing OCR'd buyer_gstin/buyer_name against COMMUNITY_GSTIN/COMMUNITY_NAME rather than a model judgment call, mirroring isOwnOrgGstin. Expanded 2026-08-29 so recipient identity is a hard requirement on every bill (low severity), while the tax-invoice ITC case stays high severity.

nodes.label: Operator decision: Haiku only, gate Sonnet auto-escalation
nodes.rationale: Sonnet was consuming too many tokens; run Haiku only until its output is reviewed on real documents before deciding whether Sonnet earns its cost.

nodes.label: Auto-escalation token bleed (I3/I10)
nodes.rationale: Escalation fired whenever contains_non_latin_script was true, which is most documents on an Indian invoice corpus, causing roughly 4x intended cost; compounded by max_tokens:2000 with no thinking parameter set, so Sonnet's adaptive thinking ate into the same budget as the tool call and truncated, forcing a full-price retry at 8000 tokens.

nodes.label: One-document-one-invoice schema assumption (I8/I12)
nodes.rationale: vendor_name/invoice_number/total_amount are flat scalars with no bills[], so an 8-bill batch scan got written into free-text notes because the schema had nowhere else to put it — a data-model bug, not a model-capability bug, confirmed by Claude's own correct notes text.

nodes.label: Unresolvable line_item_tally_mismatch on multi-bill files (I13)
nodes.rationale: Merged line-item sum compared against a single header total raises a high-severity exception every run on any multi-bill file; one document was manually re-escalated to Sonnet 7 times chasing a mismatch no model could fix under the schema.

nodes.label: bills[] schema and per-bill document_extraction rows (Phase 2)
nodes.rationale: Lets one source_document produce N document_extraction rows keyed on (source_document_id, bill_index), each independently reviewable, tally-checked and matchable to its own ledger entry, while keeping today's single-bill documents behaving exactly as before.

nodes.label: Review queue keyed by sourceDocumentId, not per-bill id (I18)
nodes.rationale: The ?id= param and prev/next navigation break the moment one document appears more than once in v_review_queue once multi-bill extraction ships; fixed by switching to documentExtractionId.

nodes.label: Batch API never implemented (I16, Phase 3)
nodes.rationale: batch-poll.ts throws 'not implemented'; every extraction runs at the full synchronous rate instead of the 50% batch rate the original plan assumed, roughly doubling real per-page cost.

nodes.label: No sweeper for stuck claimed jobs (I15)
nodes.rationale: generate_export and rasterize_retry jobs are claimed and skipped with no completion bookkeeping, deliberately leaving the row locked for a sweeper described only in a migration comment with no found implementation.

nodes.label: Two-pass gold labeling (blind vs. correction)
nodes.rationale: 10 invoices labeled blind before any upload catch silent misses that a correction-based label cannot, because a reviewer shown 'Acm' accepts it far more often than they'd type it unprompted; the blind core exists specifically as a check against the anchoring bias of the correction-based 11.

nodes.label: npm run gold:build generation pipeline
nodes.rationale: Generates test/gold.json from gold-blind-notes.json plus the live review queue's _verified columns, blind notes taking priority per document; a pure read + overwrite with no database writes, safe to re-run any time.

nodes.label: test/gold-blind-notes.json manual entries
nodes.rationale: Hand-typed ground truth read directly from the PDF before upload; fabricating values here would make every score.ts number meaningless.
